abstract: Consider a harbour monitor deciding whether a noisy underwater recording contains a vessel. Fourier analysis reveals which tones are present, spectrograms show when they occur, and wavelets describe changes across time scales. We present a multi-representation protocol for testing whether generative AI can turn these different views into useful detection evidence. A language-model agent selects tools from numerical detector summaries; a separate convolutional network analyses two-dimensional spectrograms. The agent can request replacement of a short recording interval with generated background. A proposed cross-view score compares this replacement with an approximately matched disturbance applied to the same interval, testing the intervention relative to an editing control. This comparison does not establish physical source removal. Real recordings test vessel-presence scoring, while separate synthetic and real-excerpt insertion studies examine representations and event timing. On 1,200 deliberately balanced PORTIA test clips labelled using vessel-tracking records, average precision (AP), computed from mean-seed probabilities, was 0.5738 for the agent and 0.5906 for the development-selected wavelet detector. The agent and fixed verification had the same ensemble AP; the agent required 7.02 times as much warm batch-processing time. Every agent test path acquired all primary views and verified last, demonstrating no adaptive selection. The bounded Hilbert-Huang approximation remains exploratory after numerical failures, and repeated vessels connect all five test days, preventing independent-component uncertainty estimation. The contribution is a controlled evaluation of representation choice, generative intervention and agent control, with practical checks for deciding whether each added component justifies its computational cost.
conclusion_paragraphs: The study offers a reproducible protocol for testing how different views of an underwater recording support detection. It combines representation-specific evidence, a nuisance-adjusted verification score, constrained tool selection and measured computation. In a harbour-monitoring example, a falling vessel score after generated replacement must be compared with the effect of a control edit: both can disturb useful sound. Their contrast tests sensitivity without establishing physical source removal.

On the balanced real-data cohort, ensemble AP was 0.5738 for the agent and 0.5906 for the development-selected wavelet detector. Agent and fixed verification had the same ensemble AP, but the agent required 7.02 times as much warm batch-processing time. Every test path acquired all primary views and verified last, like an inspector following a fixed checklist. Generated evidence informed no later tool choice. The continuous verification score reduced AP by 0.0257 against its matched zero-score control. Added complexity did not improve detection or selective acquisition in this execution.

The protocol helps identify which representations and AI components merit further development. Controlled-data studies and HHT checks also distinguish predictive accuracy from evidence quality. Vessel-tracking proxies and one connected test component limit generalization. Progress requires independently annotated acoustic events, additional deployments and evidence-dependent choices whose benefits survive matched controls and measured cost.

supplement_closing_paragraph: The practical lesson is to test both what a representation predicts and whether its components remain numerically meaningful. A decomposition can reconstruct a recording accurately even when its extracted components fail convergence checks; the bounded HHT results show why reconstruction alone is insufficient. Controlled scenes provide repeatable tests of representation sensitivity and known activity intervals, while keeping construction labels distinct from natural acoustic events. These studies do not establish a reasoning-agent benefit. Interpretation remains bounded by vessel-tracking labels, artificial class balance, a fixed generator seed, one deployment and one connected test component. AP, precision and calibration are cohort-specific and do not estimate deployment performance. This combination of prediction tests and numerical checks offers a useful basis for developing more dependable acoustic representations.
